items.title: Protect vulnerable road users
items.simple: People walking, biking, skating or in wheelchairs can get badly hurt. Driving distracted or careless around them is against the law. Drive so you can avoid other people's mistakes.
items.official: Drivers also share the road with vulnerable road users including pedestrians and those on bicycles, wheel chairs, skateboards, roller skates, scooters, animals and animal-drawn vehicles. It is illegal to drive distracted and carelessly around vulnerable road users. It is your responsibility to adjust your driving to avoid others' mistakes and assure everyone's safety. Pedestrians are especially prone to serious injury when struck. Be careful around schools, playgrounds and in residential areas where people may be playing or crossing the street.

items.title: Turning? Pedestrians go first
items.simple: When you turn right or left, people walking have the right-of-way. Wait until they have crossed the street all the way. Then make your turn.
items.official: Be especially aware of pedestrians when making a right or left turn. They have the right-of-way. Allow pedestrians to completely cross the street before beginning your turn.

items.title: Never pass at a crosswalk
items.simple: Do not pass another car at a crosswalk. It is against the law. The other car may hide a person walking in front of it.
items.official: Passing at a crosswalk is illegal. You may not see pedestrians crossing the road in front of other vehicles.

items.title: Stay stopped for pedestrians
items.simple: Watch for people crossing the road. Stop and stay stopped until they have passed your lane. Do not creep forward while they are in front of you.
items.official: Be alert for pedestrians crossing the road. Stop and remain stopped until pedestrians have passed the lane in which your vehicle is stopped.

items.title: Cane or guide dog: full stop
items.simple: A cane or guide dog means the person may be blind or not see well. You must come to a full stop. Older people and people with disabilities may move slowly.
items.official: Drivers are required to come to a full stop for a pedestrian using a cane or guide dog, as this indicates blindness or vision impairment. Remember that the elderly and people with disabilities may move slowly.

items.title: Not stopping: Class 1 misdemeanor
items.simple: You must come to a full stop for people crossing the road legally. If you don't stop, you could badly hurt or kill someone. That can be a Class 1 misdemeanor.
items.official: Drivers are required to come to a full stop for pedestrians who are lawfully crossing a roadway. Failing to stop and causing serious bodily damage or death can result in a Class 1 misdemeanor.
items.mnemonic: Walkers come first. Skip the stop and hurt someone: Class 1.

items.title: Bicycles: same right-of-way
items.simple: A bike rider on the road has the same right-of-way as a car. Bike riders follow many of the same laws. Some may not know or obey the rules. Slow down near them.
items.official: Bicyclists on a roadway generally has the same right-of-way as the driver of a motor vehicle. Bicyclists are subject to many of the same laws as drivers, however, some may not know or obey the rules. Slow down when you approach bicyclists.

items.title: Bikes may use center of lane
items.simple: A bike rider may ride in the middle of the lane when needed. They may do this when about to turn left. They may also do it when the lane is too narrow to share.
items.official: Bicyclists are allowed to ride in the center of the lane, when necessary, such as when they are about to turn left or when the lane is too narrow to share side-by-side with a car.

items.title: Bikes: not on interstates
items.simple: Bike riders may use all public roads except interstates and most freeways. Watch for bikes going either way on sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way bike lanes.
items.official: Bicyclists are legally allowed on all public roads except interstates and most freeways (limited access highways). Drivers should be aware of bicyclists riding in either direction on sidewalks, shared-use paths, or two-way separated bike lanes.

items.title: Never pass in a bike lane
items.simple: Never drive in a marked bike lane to pass someone. Keep your car in your own lane. You may enter a bike lane only when you must, to turn left or right.
items.official: Using marked bicycle lanes is prohibited by motor vehicles, including while passing. (Section 2: Drivers should not drive in the bicycle lane except when necessary to turn left or right.)

items.title: Pass bikes by 3+ feet
items.simple: Pass a bike rider with at least 3 feet of space. If the lane is too narrow for 3 feet, change lanes to pass. Give bikes plenty of room and be ready to stop suddenly.
items.official: State law requires motorists to pass cyclists with at least three feet of clearance. If the lane is not wide enough to allow for a three-foot clearance, the motorist must change lanes to pass safely. Give bicyclists plenty of room when passing and be prepared to stop suddenly.

items.title: Check for bikes and motorcycles
items.simple: Bikes and motorcycles are small. They slip into your blind spot easily. Look for them before you pull out, change lanes or turn. Look again before you back up, open your door or cross an intersection.
items.official: A bicycle's small size allows it to slip into your blind spot easily. Always check for bicyclists before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up, open the door, or proceed through an intersection. A motorcycle's size allows it to slip into your blind spot easily. Always check for motorcycles before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up or proceed through an intersection.

items.title: Look twice for motorcycles
items.simple: More than half of deadly motorcycle crashes involve cars. Often the driver did not see the motorcycle until too late. Look twice. Check twice before you pull out in front of one.
items.official: More than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve automobiles. Many crashes are caused by the motorist's failure to see a motorcycle in traffic. Look twice for motorcyclists. In more than half of all crashes involving motorcycles and automobiles, the other driver didn't see the motorcycle until it was too late. Drivers are conditioned to look for four-wheeled vehicles; but they don't expect to see two-wheeled vehicles. The size of a motorcycle can cause you to misjudge the motorcycle's speed and distance. Before pulling out into traffic, check twice for motorcycles and use extra caution before you pull out in front of one.

items.title: Motorcycle: add 1 second
items.simple: Never tailgate a motorcycle. Use the normal following distance rule, then add one more second. In bad weather, double that distance.
items.official: Never tailgate a motorcycle (or any other vehicle). Allow yourself plenty of braking distance by adding an extra second to the following distance rule. In inclement weather, double this distance.
items.mnemonic: Motorcycle: plus 1 second. Bad weather: times 2.

items.title: Never share a motorcycle's lane
items.simple: A motorcycle rider uses the whole lane. Small bumps or trash on the road can make them move suddenly. Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane.
items.official: Although a motorcycle is not as wide as the lane, the rider will use the entire lane as traffic situations and road conditions change. A slight change or debris on the road surface can be a major obstacle for a motorcyclist. Expect the motorcycle to make sudden moves within the lane. Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane.

items.title: The Tide: Norfolk light rail
items.simple: Norfolk has a light rail train called The Tide. It shares the road with cars and bikes. Never drive around lowered gates. Expect a train on any track at any time.
items.official: There is a light rail train system in Norfolk called The Tide. Light rail trains share the road with motor vehicles and bicyclists, and they intersect with motor vehicle traffic at 27 locations along the 7.4 mile route. Pay attention to changing traffic patterns and always follow the roadway. Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across train tracks. Expect trains on any track at any time. Always obey signs and traffic signals.

items.title: Never stop on train tracks
items.simple: Never stop, pass or shift gears on train tracks. Cross only when there is room to get all the way over. You must clear the tracks without stopping.
items.official: Never stop, pass or shift on train tracks. Don't cross train tracks unless you have enough room to cross without stopping and can clear the tracks to a safe distance.
items.mnemonic: Clear it all, or don't start at all.

items.title: Low speed vehicles: 21-25 MPH
items.simple: A low speed vehicle has four wheels and runs on electric or gas power. Its top speed is 21 to 25 MPH.
items.official: These electrically- or gas-powered four-wheel vehicles have a maximum speed ranging from 21 to 25 MPH.

items.title: LSVs: roads 35 MPH or less
items.simple: Low speed vehicles may use roads with speed limits of 35 MPH or less. The driver needs a license. A permit holder may drive one with a licensed driver along.
items.official: Low speed vehicles may be operated on public roads with speed limits of 35 MPH or less by licensed drivers or learner's permit holders accompanied by a licensed driver. Low speed vehicles must comply with all federal safety standards and must meet Virginia's requirements for passenger vehicle registration and insurance coverage.

items.title: Golf carts are not LSVs
items.simple: A golf cart is not a low speed vehicle. Don't mix them up. Low speed vehicles have four wheels. Their top speed is 21 to 25 MPH.
items.official: Golf carts are not classified as low speed vehicles.

items.title: Truck No-Zones
items.simple: Trucks, buses and RVs have danger areas around them called No-Zones. They are on the sides, front and back. The driver may not see you there. Stay out of No-Zones.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and recreational vehicles (RVs) are longer, higher and wider than other vehicles. They accelerate slowly and require greater stopping and turning distances. Plus, there are danger areas around these vehicles where crashes are more likely to occur. These areas are called No-Zones. No-Zones on the side, front and rear also include blind spots where your car disappears from the driver's view.

items.title: Mirror rule: see the driver's face
items.simple: Trucks have big blind spots on both sides. Look at the truck's side mirror. If you cannot see the driver's face in it, the driver cannot see you.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and RVs have big No-Zones on both sides that are dangerous because these vehicles must make wide turns. These No-Zones or blind spots are much larger than your car's blind spots. If you can't see the driver's face in his side view mirror, then he can't see you.
items.mnemonic: See his face, or leave that place.

items.title: Rear No-Zone: don't tailgate trucks
items.simple: A truck driver cannot see your car right behind the truck. You cannot see traffic ahead of it. If the truck stops fast, you have nowhere to go. Keep a safe following distance.
items.official: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and RVs have huge No-Zones directly behind them. The driver can't see your car behind his vehicle and you can't see what's happening in traffic ahead of his vehicle. If the truck, bus or RV brakes or stops suddenly, you have no place to go and could crash into the vehicle's rear-end. Always maintain a safe following distance.

items.title: Passing a truck: see its front
items.simple: After you pass a truck, do not cut in too soon. Wait until you see the whole front of the truck in your rearview mirror. Then pull in and keep your speed.
items.official: You could get rear-ended by a truck, bus or RV if you cut in front too soon after passing the vehicle or if you cut in front and then suddenly slow down. When passing, look for the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror before pulling in front. And then, maintain your speed.
items.mnemonic: Whole truck front in the mirror? Now pull in.

items.title: Trucks need twice the stopping room
items.simple: Trucks, buses and RVs are slow to stop. They need nearly twice the time and room a car needs. If you cut in and slow down, the truck may not stop in time.
items.official: These vehicles need nearly twice the time and room to stop as cars.

items.title: Truck length and passing room
items.simple: A truck and its trailer can be up to 65 feet long. Passing one can take more than half a mile of clear road. Be sure you have the room before you pass.
items.official: A truck and its trailer may be as long as 65 feet and it may take you more than half a mile of clear road to pass.
items.mnemonic: 65 feet long, half a mile to pass.

items.title: Trucks swing wide to turn
items.simple: Big trucks, buses and RVs may swing wide to the left or right to turn. They can't see cars right behind or beside them. Never squeeze between a truck and the curb or another car.
items.official: Trucks, buses and RVs sometimes need to swing wide to the left or right to safely make a turn. They can't see the cars directly behind or beside them. Never try to squeeze between a truck, bus or RV and the curb or another vehicle.

items.title: Blind spots: 20 front, 200 back
items.simple: A truck's blind spot can reach up to 20 feet in front of the cab. Behind the truck, it can reach about 200 feet. Stay out of them.
items.official: In fact, their blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab and approximately 200 feet behind the vehicle.
items.mnemonic: 20 in front, 200 behind. Add a zero for the back.

items.title: Towing: twice as long
items.simple: Towing a trailer puts extra stress on your vehicle. It takes twice as long to pass, stop, speed up and turn. Large side mirrors help you see. Remember the No-Zones.
items.official: These trailers are attached to mid-sized cars and trucks with safety chains and a trailer hitch. Large side mirrors are generally needed to increase visibility. Towing a trailer places additional stress on the vehicle; it takes the vehicle twice as long to pass, stop, accelerate and turn.

items.title: Trailer safety check every trip
items.simple: Check your trailer before every trip. Make sure the hitch pin, coupler and safety chains are secure. Check the plug and all the lights. Practice first in an empty parking lot.
items.official: Before driving a vehicle with a light to medium trailer attached, perform a safety inspection before each trip. Ensure: the pin securing the ball mount to the receiver is intact; the hitch coupler is secured; safety chains are properly attached; the electrical plug is properly installed; brake lights, turn signals, and license plate lights are functioning properly. Before pulling a trailer on public roads, find a location such as a vacant parking lot to practice.

items.title: Trailer sways? Slow down
items.simple: If your trailer starts to sway, slow down. Your trailer makes your vehicle longer. Allow for that extra length when you change lanes.
items.official: When driving a vehicle with a light to medium trailer attached: always allow for the added length of the trailer when you change lanes; if your trailer starts to sway, slow down.

items.title: Backing a trailer: hand at bottom
items.simple: To back up a trailer, put your hand on the bottom of the steering wheel. Move the wheel left to send the trailer left. Move it right to send it right. Can't see? Get a helper.
items.official: When backing up, place your hand on the bottom of the steering wheel. If you cannot see where you are backing up, have someone outside to help guide you. To back the trailer to the left, use your left hand to move the wheel left. To back the trailer to the right, use your right hand to move the wheel to the right.
items.mnemonic: Hand at the bottom: the trailer goes where your hand goes.

questions.explain: A cane or guide dog means the person is blind or has a vision impairment.

questions.prompt: Which pedestrians may move slowly when crossing the street?
choices: The elderly and people with disabilities
questions.explain: Remember that the elderly and people with disabilities may move slowly.

questions.prompt: Failing to stop for a pedestrian lawfully crossing, and causing serious injury or death, can result in:
questions.explain: Failing to stop and causing serious bodily injury or death can result in a Class 1 misdemeanor.

questions.prompt: Drivers are required to come to a full stop for pedestrians who are:
questions.explain: You must come to a full stop for pedestrians lawfully crossing a roadway.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist riding on the roadway generally has:
choices: The right-of-way only in bike lanes
The same right-of-way as a motor vehicle driver
questions.explain: Bicyclists on a roadway generally have the same right-of-way as drivers of motor vehicles.

questions.prompt: When you approach a bicyclist, you should:
questions.explain: Slow down when you approach bicyclists; some may not know or obey the rules.

questions.prompt: This sign warns of bicycles. On the road, a bicyclist generally has:
choices: No right to use the road
The same right-of-way as a car
questions.explain: Bicyclists on the road generally have the same right-of-way as motor vehicles.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist may ride in the center of the lane when:
choices: They are riding on an interstate
The lane is too narrow to share side-by-side with a car
Never; bicyclists must always ride on the shoulder
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride in the center of the lane when necessary, such as when the lane is too narrow to share.

questions.prompt: You see this marking. A bicyclist ahead is riding in the middle of your narrow lane. This is:
choices: Allowed when the lane is too narrow to share
Illegal; the bicyclist must move to the curb
questions.explain: Bicyclists may use the center of the lane when it is too narrow to share side-by-side with a car.

questions.prompt: A bicyclist moves to the center of the lane just before an intersection. The rider is probably:
questions.explain: Bicyclists may ride in the center of the lane when they are about to turn left.

questions.prompt: Bicyclists are legally allowed on all public roads except:
questions.explain: Bicyclists may use all public roads except interstates and most freeways.

questions.prompt: On sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way separated bike lanes, expect bicyclists:
choices: Only going the same way as traffic
Never; bicycles must stay on the road
questions.explain: Be aware of bicyclists riding in either direction on sidewalks, shared-use paths and two-way bike lanes.

questions.prompt: Driving a motor vehicle in this marked lane to pass another car is:
choices: Allowed if no bicycles are in it
Allowed if you use your turn signal
questions.explain: Motor vehicles may not use marked bicycle lanes, including while passing.

questions.prompt: Which is true about marked bicycle lanes?
choices: Cars may not use them, even to pass
Cars may use them to pass slow traffic
Cars may park in them for short stops
Cars may use them when they are empty
questions.explain: Using marked bicycle lanes is prohibited for motor vehicles, including while passing.

questions.prompt: When passing a bicyclist, Virginia law requires at least:
questions.explain: State law requires passing bicyclists with at least three feet of clearance.

questions.prompt: If a lane is too narrow to pass a bicyclist with three feet of clearance, you must:
choices: Pass anyway at a slow speed
Use the bike lane to pass
Honk so the bicyclist moves onto the shoulder
questions.explain: If the lane is not wide enough for three feet of clearance, change lanes to pass.

questions.prompt: You see this sign and a bicyclist ahead. When you pass, you must leave at least:
questions.explain: Pass bicyclists with at least three feet of clearance.

questions.prompt: You should always check for bicyclists before you:
questions.explain: Always check for bicyclists before you pull out, change lanes, turn, back up, open the door or go through an intersection.

questions.prompt: Bicycles and motorcycles are easy to miss because:
choices: They always ride on the sidewalk
Their small size lets them slip into your blind spot
They are only on the road at night
questions.explain: A bicycle's or motorcycle's small size allows it to slip into your blind spot easily.

questions.prompt: A motorcycle can easily hide in the area shown. Before you change lanes, you should:
choices: Speed up and change lanes quickly
Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder
questions.explain: Motorcycles slip into blind spots easily, so check over your shoulder before changing lanes.

questions.prompt: More than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve:
questions.explain: More than half of all fatal motorcycle crashes involve automobiles.

questions.prompt: In more than half of crashes between motorcycles and cars, the car driver:
choices: Did not see the motorcycle until it was too late
questions.explain: In more than half of these crashes, the other driver didn't see the motorcycle until it was too late.

questions.prompt: Before pulling out into traffic, you should check for motorcycles:
choices: Never; they will yield to you
questions.explain: Check twice for motorcycles and use extra caution before pulling out in front of one.

questions.prompt: Why is it easy to misjudge a motorcycle's speed and distance?
questions.explain: The size of a motorcycle can cause you to misjudge its speed and distance.

questions.prompt: When following a motorcycle, you should:
choices: Follow closer so the rider can see you
Follow closer because motorcycles stop slowly
Flash your lights so the rider moves over
Add an extra second to the following distance rule
questions.explain: Allow plenty of braking distance by adding an extra second to the following distance rule.

questions.prompt: When following a motorcycle in bad weather, you should:
choices: Cut your following distance in half
questions.explain: In inclement weather, double the following distance behind a motorcycle.

questions.prompt: Which is true about sharing a lane with a motorcycle?
choices: You may drive beside it because it is narrow
You may share the lane if you signal
Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane
You may share the lane on highways
questions.explain: Never drive beside a motorcycle in the same lane.

questions.prompt: Why might a motorcycle make sudden moves within its lane?
choices: Debris or small changes in the road surface
To let cars share the lane
questions.explain: A slight change or debris on the road can be a major obstacle for a motorcyclist.

questions.prompt: At this light rail crossing, the gates are down. You must:
choices: Stop and never drive around the lowered gates
Drive around the gates if no train is in sight
questions.explain: Never drive around lowered crossing gates.

questions.prompt: The Tide is a light rail train system in:
questions.explain: There is a light rail train system in Norfolk called The Tide.

questions.prompt: When driving near light rail tracks, you should:
choices: Expect trains only during rush hour
Expect trains only on the left track
Assume the train will stop for you
Expect trains on any track at any time
questions.explain: Expect trains on any track at any time.

questions.prompt: When crossing light rail or train tracks, you should never:
choices: Stop, pass or shift gears on the tracks
Cross when you have room to clear the tracks
questions.explain: Never stop, pass or shift on train tracks.

questions.prompt: You should not start across train tracks unless:
choices: The car ahead is already on the tracks
You have room to cross without stopping and clear the tracks
questions.explain: Don't cross train tracks unless you have enough room to cross without stopping and clear them.

questions.prompt: Traffic ahead is stopped just past this crossing. You should:
choices: Wait before the tracks until there is room to clear them
Stop on the tracks behind the last car
Pass the stopped cars on the tracks
questions.explain: Never stop on train tracks; cross only when you can clear them.

questions.prompt: Low speed vehicles have a maximum speed of:
questions.explain: Low speed vehicles have a maximum speed ranging from 21 to 25 MPH.

questions.prompt: A low speed vehicle is:
choices: A four-wheel electric or gas vehicle with a top speed of 21 to 25 MPH
questions.explain: Low speed vehicles are electric- or gas-powered four-wheel vehicles with a top speed of 21 to 25 MPH.

questions.prompt: Low speed vehicles may be driven on public roads with speed limits of:
questions.explain: Low speed vehicles may be operated on public roads with speed limits of 35 MPH or less.

questions.prompt: Which statement about low speed vehicles is true?

A learner's permit holder may drive one with a licensed driver along
They may be driven on interstates
They are the same as golf carts
questions.explain: Licensed drivers, or learner's permit holders accompanied by a licensed driver, may operate low speed vehicles.

questions.prompt: Low speed vehicles must meet Virginia's requirements for:
questions.explain: Low speed vehicles must meet Virginia's requirements for passenger vehicle registration and insurance.

questions.prompt: Golf carts are:
choices: Not classified as low speed vehicles
questions.explain: Golf carts are not classified as low speed vehicles.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a low speed vehicle?
choices: A four-wheel electric vehicle with a top speed of 25 MPH
A four-wheel gas vehicle with a top speed of 21 MPH
A four-wheel electric vehicle with a top speed of 23 MPH
questions.explain: Golf carts are not classified as low speed vehicles.

questions.prompt: The shaded areas around this truck are called:
questions.explain: Danger areas around trucks, buses and RVs where crashes are more likely are called No-Zones.

questions.prompt: Compared to cars, trucks, buses and RVs:
choices: Speed up faster and stop in less distance
Speed up slowly and need more distance to stop and turn
Can always see cars behind them
questions.explain: These vehicles accelerate slowly and require greater stopping and turning distances.

questions.prompt: If you cannot see a truck driver's face in his side view mirror:
choices: You are at a safe distance
The truck driver can see you clearly
The truck driver cannot see you
You should stay there and honk
questions.explain: If you can't see the driver's face in his side view mirror, then he can't see you.

questions.prompt: The blind spots on the sides of trucks, buses and RVs are:
choices: Much larger than a car's blind spots
Smaller than a car's blind spots
The same as a car's blind spots
questions.explain: Side No-Zones on large vehicles are much larger than your car's blind spots.

questions.prompt: Following too closely behind a truck is dangerous because:
choices: Trucks stop in less distance than cars
The truck driver can always see you in the mirror
The truck driver can't see you and you can't see traffic ahead
questions.explain: In the rear No-Zone the driver can't see you and you can't see traffic ahead of the truck.

questions.prompt: Trucks, buses and RVs have a huge No-Zone:
choices: Nowhere, because they have large mirrors
questions.explain: Trucks, buses and RVs have huge No-Zones directly behind them.

questions.prompt: After passing a truck, you should pull back in front of it when:
choices: Your back bumper passes its front bumper
The truck driver flashes his lights
You are one car length ahead
You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror
questions.explain: Look for the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror before pulling in front.

questions.prompt: After you pass a truck and pull in front of it, you should:
questions.explain: After pulling in front of a truck, maintain your speed.

questions.prompt: You could be rear-ended by a truck if you:
choices: Cut in too soon after passing it
Cut in front and then suddenly slow down
questions.explain: Cutting in too soon or cutting in and then slowing down can get you rear-ended by a truck.

questions.prompt: Compared to cars, trucks, buses and RVs need about how much time and room to stop?
questions.explain: These vehicles need nearly twice the time and room to stop as cars.

questions.prompt: Why is it dangerous to cut in front of a large truck and then slow down?
choices: The truck can stop faster than you
Trucks have smaller blind spots than cars
The truck needs nearly twice the room to stop as a car
questions.explain: Trucks need nearly twice the time and room to stop as cars.

questions.prompt: A truck and its trailer may be as long as:
questions.explain: A truck and its trailer may be as long as 65 feet.

questions.prompt: Passing a truck may take you more than ___ of clear road.
questions.explain: It may take more than half a mile of clear road to pass a truck.

questions.prompt: A truck ahead is swinging wide to make a right turn. You should:
choices: Stay back and never squeeze between the truck and the curb
Squeeze between the truck and the curb
questions.explain: Never try to squeeze between a truck, bus or RV and the curb or another vehicle.

questions.prompt: Trucks, buses and RVs sometimes swing wide when turning because:
choices: They need the room to turn safely
questions.explain: These vehicles sometimes need to swing wide to the left or right to safely make a turn.

questions.prompt: A truck's blind spot may stretch up to how far in front of the cab?
questions.explain: Truck blind spots may stretch up to 20 feet in front of the cab.

questions.prompt: A large truck's blind spot behind it may stretch approximately:
questions.explain: Truck blind spots may stretch approximately 200 feet behind the vehicle.

questions.prompt: Towing a light to medium trailer makes it take how long to pass, stop, accelerate and turn?
questions.explain: Towing a trailer makes it take twice as long to pass, stop, accelerate and turn.

questions.prompt: Light to medium trailers are attached to a vehicle with:
choices: Safety chains and a trailer hitch
questions.explain: These trailers are attached with safety chains and a trailer hitch.

questions.prompt: Before each trip with a trailer, you should check that:
choices: The safety chains are properly attached
The brake lights and turn signals work
questions.explain: Before each trip, check the hitch pin, coupler, safety chains, electrical plug and lights.

questions.prompt: Before pulling a trailer on public roads, it is a good idea to:
choices: Practice in a place like a vacant parking lot
questions.explain: Practice in a location such as a vacant parking lot before towing on public roads.

questions.prompt: A trailer safety inspection should be done:
questions.explain: Perform a trailer safety inspection before each trip.

questions.prompt: If the trailer you are towing starts to sway, you should:
questions.explain: If your trailer starts to sway, slow down.

questions.prompt: When changing lanes while towing a trailer, you should:
choices: Allow for the added length of the trailer
questions.explain: Always allow for the added length of the trailer when you change lanes.

questions.prompt: When backing up with a trailer, place your hand:
choices: On the top of the steering wheel
On the bottom of the steering wheel
questions.explain: When backing up with a trailer, place your hand on the bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.prompt: To back a trailer to the right, you should:
choices: Use your left hand to move the wheel left
Use your right hand to move the wheel to the right
Turn the wheel hard left with both hands
questions.explain: To back the trailer to the right, use your right hand to move the wheel to the right.

questions.prompt: If you cannot see where you are backing up with a trailer, you should:
choices: Sound your horn and keep backing
Have someone outside help guide you
questions.explain: If you cannot see where you are backing up, have someone outside help guide you.

questions.prompt: When passing a bicyclist, you should give plenty of room and be prepared to:
questions.explain: Give bicyclists plenty of room when passing and be prepared to stop suddenly.

questions.prompt: Which of these vehicles have No-Zones where your car can disappear from the driver's view?
questions.explain: Trucks, tractor-trailers, buses and RVs, such as motor homes and campers, all have No-Zones.

questions.prompt: When driving around The Tide light rail, you should:
choices: Pay attention to changing traffic patterns and follow the roadway
Drive on the tracks to pass traffic
Ignore signals when no train is near
questions.explain: Pay attention to changing traffic patterns and always follow the roadway near The Tide.

questions.prompt: You should be especially careful near schools, playgrounds and residential areas because:
choices: People may be playing or crossing the street
questions.explain: Be careful around schools, playgrounds and residential areas where people may be playing or crossing the street.
